 CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS:  We will hear
 argument this morning in Case 25-581, St. Mary
 Catholic Parish versus Roy.
 Mr. Reaves.
 ORAL ARGUMENT OF NICHOLAS R. REAVES
 ON BEHALF OF THE PETITIONERS
 MR. REAVES: Mr. Chief Justice, and
may it please the Court:
 The Archdiocese of Denver schools
exist to pass on the faith to the next
 generation.  To do this, they ask all families
who enroll to be open to and supportive of the
 church's teachings.  Because of this sincere
religious exercise, the State has denied
 Colorado families the ability to use Universal
 Preschool funding at Catholic schools.  Under
this Court's public benefits cases, that
 triggers strict scrutiny.
 The Tenth Circuit was wrong to cabin
that precedent that this Court reaffirmed in
Carson to explicit religious exclusions only.
 That can't be reconciled with Sherbert, Thomas,
or Mahmoud. Nor can it be reconciled with this

operation and the effect of the law, not for
 magic words.
 After rejecting Carson, the Tenth
Circuit applied Smith, but this too was wrong.
When Colorado allows over a thousand schools to
turn families away for a variety of different
 reasons, it has created a flexible and
 customizable program, nothing like the
 generally applicable across-the-board laws that
 Smith envisioned.
 And Colorado's inconsistent and
contradictory arguments further confirm the
 State's actions are anything but generally

the mandate to accommodate important secular
interests, but it's called the same law a hard
 limit when Petitioners sought a religious
 accommodation.
 And Colorado has discretion via the
 catch-all exemption to permit preschools to
 organize around "specific competencies or
 interests" and to serve "specific communities."
Yet it has refused to extend that flexible
 treatment to Petitioners.
